title: digitalis purpurea f. nevadensis
intro: Digitalis purpurea f. nevadensis, commonly known as Western foxglove, is a subspecies of the Foxglove plant (Digitalis purpurea), characterized by its unique growth patterns and medicinal properties. Western foxglove has been utilized in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including the treatment of heart conditions, such as arrhythmias and congestive heart failure, due to its ability to increase cardiac contractility and slow heart rate. The therapeutic actions of Western foxglove can be attributed to its bioactive constituents, including digoxin, digoxigenin, and digitoxigenin, which work together to exert cardiotonic and inotropic effects. However, due to its potential toxicity, the use of Western foxglove should be strictly regulated and under the guidance of a medical professional.
